participantInstructions: The Business Law and Ethics Team Decision Making Event is presented to you through the 21st Century Skills, the Performance Indicators, and the situation on the following pages. You will have 30 minutes to read this situation and prepare your presentation. You will then have up to 15 minutes to make your presentation to the judge and to answer the judge's questions; no additional time beyond the 15 minutes is allotted for questions. Both members of your team must take part in the presentation and in answering the judge's questions. You will be evaluated on how well you meet each performance indicator. All of your notes and materials will be turned in at the end of the event.
situation:
You are the customer relations manager and the operations coordinator at APEXCORE REMANUFACTURING, a rebuilder of starters, alternators, and brake calipers sold to auto parts retailers and independent repair shops. The general manager (judge) was hired eight months ago to reverse two consecutive years of shrinking margins and has asked your team to review a plan for the company's walk-in core exchange counter, the point where retail customers bring in used parts for inspection and credit.

APEXCORE built its reputation on that counter. Trained core advisors meet each customer in person, inspect the returned part, explain how it is graded, and issue credit on the spot, a service competitors mostly handle through anonymous mail-in programs. That personal review also catches grading disputes before they become refund battles, which keeps warranty costs down. Rising core costs and slow counter throughput have eaten into margins for two years, and leadership has committed publicly to cutting counter wait times by half before the next fiscal year begins.

To meet that target, the general manager (judge) has proposed replacing counter staff with a self-service kiosk that scans a core's barcode and prints a credit voucher without an advisor present. The kiosk would cut labor cost per transaction sharply and move customers through in minutes instead of an average of eighteen. But the current kiosk design mounts its touchscreen at standing height, offers no audio prompts, and requires customers to read grading codes off a printed chart, features a blind or wheelchair-using customer cannot use unassisted.

Removing advisors from the counter would also remove the face-to-face inspection that customers say they trust and that competitors cannot easily copy; APEXCORE's own customer surveys cite that interaction, not price, as the top reason customers choose the company over mail-in rivals. A hybrid option, keeping one advisor on the floor to assist any customer the kiosk cannot serve, protects access but preserves less of the projected labor savings, and the general manager (judge) has already told the board a specific throughput number.

The general manager (judge) wants your team to recommend how APEXCORE should redesign the counter experience: whether to proceed with the kiosk as designed, retrofit it for accessible use, keep the counter fully staffed, or adopt a hybrid model, and how the change would be communicated to counter staff and rolled into their daily work rules. Whatever you recommend must serve every customer who walks in, not only the ones a kiosk can serve.

The general manager (judge) will greet you both at the start of the meeting and ask to hear your team's recommendation and reasoning. Be prepared to discuss how your plan would actually be put into practice at the counter. The general manager will thank you both for your presentation and for answering questions once the meeting concludes.

You were hired eight months ago to reverse two consecutive years of shrinking margins, and you have proposed replacing the staffed walk-in core counter with a self-service kiosk to cut wait times in half, a number you have already given the board. You want the participants to recommend whether to proceed with the kiosk as designed, retrofit it for accessible use, keep the counter fully staffed, or adopt a hybrid model, and to tell you how their recommendation would actually work at the counter.
